what_its_for: This combination medicine is used on the skin to help soothe minor skin irritation, itching, and discomfort. Allantoin helps moisturize and soften the skin to promote healing, while benzethonium chloride works as an antiseptic to help prevent infection in minor cuts, scrapes, burns, and skin irritations.
how_to_take: This medicine is for use on the skin only — do not swallow it. Clean the affected area gently with mild soap and water, then pat it dry. Apply a small amount of the medicine directly to the irritated or affected skin area. Wash your hands before and after applying the medicine, unless you are treating your hands. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages unless your doctor tells you to. Do not use inside the nose, mouth, eyes, or ears unless your doctor specifically tells you it is safe to do so.
dosing: For most adults and children 2 years and older: Apply to the affected skin area up to 3 to 4 times per day, or as directed on the product label. Use only the smallest amount needed to cover and soothe the affected area. Do not use more often than recommended. For children under 2 years of age, ask your doctor or pharmacist before use.
missed_dose: Since this medicine is used as needed for skin irritation, there is no set dosing schedule to follow. If you forget to apply a dose, just apply it when you remember. Do not apply extra medicine to make up for a missed application. Simply continue with your regular routine.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from direct sunlight, heat, and moisture. Do not freeze. Keep the cap or lid tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not get this medicine in your eyes, mouth, nose, or ears. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with clean water. Avoid using this medicine on large areas of skin that are deeply wounded, infected, or severely burned without first talking to your doctor. Do not use on skin that has a rash from poison ivy, poison oak, or poison sumac without checking with your doctor first. Avoid using other skin products on the same area at the same time unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical attention if: the condition gets worse or does not improve within 7 days of use; you develop a rash, severe redness, swelling, or blistering at the application site; you notice signs of a serious skin infection such as increased warmth, pus, or red streaking; you accidentally swallow any of the medicine; you have an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
when_it_works: Most people begin to feel soothing relief of itching and irritation within a short time of applying the medicine, often within minutes to a few hours. Minor skin healing may take a few days with regular use. If you do not see improvement within 7 days, speak with your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should ask their doctor or pharmacist before using this medicine, especially on large areas of skin. For children under 2 years of age, always check with a doctor before use. Older adults may have more sensitive skin and should use the smallest effective amount to avoid irritation.
